Chief_Complaint.content: Anxious about worsening symptoms after insect sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Sting occurred on right arm a few minutes prior to evaluation
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Sting on right arm a few minutes ago

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is uncertain whether the sting was from a bee or wasp
Localized redness with puncture mark at sting site
No current severe airway symptoms reported but apprehensive about progression
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: no current severe airway symptoms but apprehensive about progression

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Currently not in acute respiratory distress
Patient asked about need for urgent care for current symptoms
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: he asks about need for urgent care

History_of_Present_Illness.content: No known prior history of anaphylaxis
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Anaphylaxis history: Not known; no prior anaphylaxis.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen) has not been prescribed and has not been used
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: EpiPen: Not used; has not been prescribed.

Medications.content: Piriton (chlorphenamine) 4 mg by mouth every 6 hours as needed up to approximately 6 times per day recommended
Medications.source_text: Piriton (chlorphenamine) 4 mg PO every 6 hours as needed (up to ~6 times/day)

Medications.content: Alternative dosing option of Piriton: 1 tablet daily if preferred
No prescription needed for Piriton recommendation

Assessment.content: Localized allergic or inflammatory reaction to insect sting on right arm, likely bee or wasp, without current anaphylaxis
Assessment.source_text: Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to insect sting (likely bee/wasp) on right arm; no current anaphylaxis.

Plan_of_Care.content: Use over-the-counter antihistamine such as Piriton (chlorphenamine) as discussed
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
Antihistamine: OTC options discussed.
  – Piriton (chlorphenamine) 4 mg PO every 6 hours as needed (up to ~6 times/day), or
  – 1 tablet daily if preferred.

Plan_of_Care.content: Monitor sting site for spread of redness, warmth, or signs of infection
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Monitor for spread of redness, warmth, or infection

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider antibiotics if signs of infection develop at sting site
Patient advised to go to emergency department immediately for worsening or new lip or tongue swelling, tongue or throat closing, facial or airway edema, or difficulty breathing or stridor
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
Red flags (go to ED immediately):
  – Worsening or new lip/tongue swelling, tongue/throat closing, facial/or airway edema, or difficulty breathing/stridor.

Plan_of_Care.content: No allergy testing needed at this time
Plan_of_Care.source_text: No allergy testing needed at this time

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider allergy testing if recurrent non-specific rashes occur in the future
Plan_of_Care.source_text: consider if recurrent non-specific rashes in future.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient provided with information link on anaphylaxis
Patient reassured that current presentation is a localized reaction
Plan_of_Care.source_text: reassured that current presentation is a localized reaction

Plan_of_Care.content: Instructions given to seek care if symptoms worsen
Plan_of_Care.source_text: instructions to seek care if symptoms worsen.

Follow_up_Information.content: Return if symptoms deteriorate or do not improve with antihistamines
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Return if symptoms deteriorate or do not improve with antihistamines

Follow_up_Information.content: No routine follow-up needed if symptoms improve
